# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 63 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 63 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_063_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter serves as a transitional passage between Similitude 5 and Similitude 6. It contains a rare personal disclosure by Hermas: he has maintained sexual purity throughout his life (*apo gynaikos...emeautou etērēsa*). The Shepherd's commendation and then extension — "you must also guard the flesh holy and undefiled" — suggests that Hermas's self-assessment may be incomplete or that the standard is higher than mere sexual purity.

The phrase "the Spirit that dwells in it may bear witness to it" is a remarkable pneumatological claim: the Holy Spirit's presence in the flesh is testimonial — the Spirit witnesses to the flesh's purity before God.

EMET's "glad" for the commandments in 63:1 is unusual — LOGOS uses "glad" too. The Greek *hilara* = cheerful/merry/glad. All three translate it similarly; SOPHIA uses "glad" as appropriate.

---

## Similitude 6 Transition — Keep the Flesh Pure

**63:1** As I was sitting at home and glorifying God for all that I had seen, and meditating on the commandments — how they were beautiful and powerful and glad and glorious and able to save the soul of a man — I said to myself: I shall be blessed if I walk in these commandments, and blessed shall be all who walk in them.

**63:2** While I was saying these things to myself, I saw him sitting beside me and saying: "Why are you double-minded about the commandments that I gave you? They are beautiful. Do not be in any doubt, but clothe yourself with the faith of the Lord and walk in them, for I will strengthen you in them."

**63:3** "This commandment especially pleases me, lord," I said, "for I have never in my life sinned against it." "Speak," he said. "I have always," I said, "even to this day, kept myself chaste — from women and from every kind of adultery and impurity." He rejoiced at this and said: "Good — you say this because you have done well in this. But I will tell you one more thing: you must also guard the flesh pure and undefiled, so that the Spirit that dwells in it may bear witness to it, and your flesh may be justified."

**63:4** "Take care," he said, "lest any thought enter your heart concerning this flesh of yours and you consider it defiled. For if the pure flesh is defiled by an evil thought, it brings death. But keep it pure and believe: if you keep the flesh pure, you shall live to God."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
